chapter.title: Plugging in your work apps

cards.body: Some stations on your line need to reach into another building: the spreadsheet in Google Sheets, the channel in Slack. They can't just walk in. A **credential is a key card** you cut once and hang by the door, and any station that needs that building grabs the same card.
cards.simpler: Think of your workflow as a line of stations. Some stations need to reach into another building, like the spreadsheet in Google Sheets or the channel in Slack. They can't just walk in. A **credential is a key card** you make once and hang by the door. Any station that needs that building grabs the same card.

cards.prompt: Priya builds a line with two Slack stations: one posts to #sales, the other posts to #ops. How many Slack key cards does she need to cut?

options.text: One, both stations grab the same card.
One per channel, so two, plus a spare.

whyNot.a: That's one card per station, but the card opens Slack, not a station: both stations share it.
whyNot.c: That's a card per channel, but the card opens the whole of Slack: the channel is just a setting on the station.

cards.reteach: A credential belongs to an app, not to a box on your canvas. Cut one Slack card and every Slack node you ever add can pick it from a list. You only cut a second card if you want n8n to act as a different person or team.

cards.title: What a credential is
cards.body:
A *credential* is n8n's saved permission to act as you inside one app. For Google Sheets that usually means clicking Sign in with Google and pressing Allow. For Slack it's a sign-in too, or a long secret string the app gives you. n8n stores it, and you never type it again.

Every app node has a box near the top labelled Credential to connect with. Empty box, no entry. Pick a card from the list, or choose Create new, and the station can get in.

**Make it once, pick it everywhere.** The card lives on the Credentials page in the left sidebar, not inside any single workflow.
cards.simpler: A credential is n8n's saved permission to act as you inside one app. For Google Sheets, you sign in and press Allow. Slack is a sign-in too, or a long secret code from the app. n8n keeps it, and you never type it again. Each app node has a Credential box. Pick a card there, or choose Create new. **Make it once, pick it everywhere.** The card lives on the Credentials page in the left sidebar, not inside any workflow.

cards.title: Sam and the pop-up
cards.body: Sam adds a Google Sheets node to log new leads. The node asks for a credential, so he clicks Create new. A Google window pops up, he picks his work account, presses Allow, and the window closes on its own. Back in n8n the dropdown now shows his email, and the sheet picker fills with his real spreadsheets, including one called 'DO NOT DELETE v3'. He never typed a password into n8n: Google handed it a key, and n8n hung it by the door.
cards.simpler: Sam adds a Google Sheets node to log new leads. The node asks for a credential, so he clicks Create new. A Google window opens. He picks his work account and presses Allow, and the window closes by itself. Back in n8n, the dropdown shows his email, and the sheet picker lists his spreadsheets, including one called 'DO NOT DELETE v3'. **He never typed a password into n8n.** Google handed it a key, and n8n hung it by the door.

cards.prompt: Dev adds a second Google Sheets node to the same workflow, to read a different spreadsheet. Its credential box is empty. What should he do?

options.text: Click Create new and sign in to Google again, since it's a new spreadsheet.
Open the dropdown and pick the Google account he already connected.
Paste the first node's spreadsheet link into the credential box.

whyNot.a: That's cutting a second card, but the first one already opens every sheet his account can see: a new sheet doesn't need a new sign-in.
whyNot.c: That's the station's job setting, which sheet to use, not the key card that gets it through the door.

cards.reteach: The credential box asks 'who is n8n acting as?', not 'which file?'. One Google sign-in covers every spreadsheet that account can open. Pick the existing card, then choose the sheet in the fields below it.

cards.title: Pick the job, then press test
cards.body:
Once the card is in, each app station does **one job you choose from a list**. In Google Sheets that's an *operation*: append a row, read rows, update a row. In Slack it's send a message. Pick the operation, then fill in the blanks: which sheet, which channel, what text.

Press the test button on the station. It really adds the row or really sends the message, so aim it at a test sheet or a channel only you are in. Then read the output panel from chapter 2: a green result means the card worked and the job ran.

If the test fails with words like unauthorized or forbidden, it's the card, not your fields.
cards.simpler: Once the card is in, each app station does **one job you choose from a list**. Add a row in Google Sheets, or send a message in Slack. Then fill in the blanks: which sheet, what text. Press test. It really runs, so aim it at a test sheet or a channel only you are in. A green result means the card worked. If it fails with words like unauthorized or forbidden, the card is the problem, not your fields.

cards.body: Lena's Slack node fails with a permissions error. She rebuilds the whole workflow, twice, and it still fails. The nodes were fine. The key card was cut with an account that isn't in the #ops channel. **When an app node can't get in, check the card first**: open the Credentials page and see whose account it is and whether it still works.
cards.simpler: Lena's Slack node fails with a permissions error. She rebuilds the whole workflow, twice, and it still fails. The nodes were never the problem. The key card was made with an account that is not in the #ops channel. **When an app node can't get in, check the card first.** Open the Credentials page, see whose account it is, and check that it still works.

cards.prompt: Which of these lives on the Credentials page, outside any single workflow?

options.text: The sheet name a Google Sheets node writes to.
Your saved Google sign-in that any Google Sheets node can pick.
The output panel showing what the node sent on.

whyNot.a: That's a setting on one station, filled in inside the workflow.
whyNot.c: That's the belt from chapter 2, what a station hands to the next, shown inside a run.

cards.reteach: Think of three layers. The workflow is the line, the node is a station, and the credential is the key card hanging by the door. Only the card lives outside the workflow, so one card serves every line you ever build.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body: A credential is a key card: you sign in to an app once and n8n keeps the permission. Every node for that app picks the same card from a list, then does **one job** like adding a row or sending a message.
cards.simpler: A credential is a key card. You sign in to an app once, and n8n keeps the permission. Every node for that app picks the same card from a list, then does **one job**, like adding a row or sending a message.

cards.body: Tonight: open n8n, click Credentials in the left sidebar, and connect one app you use at work. Add that app's node to a workflow, pick the card, and send one test message to yourself.
cards.simpler: Tonight, open n8n and click Credentials in the left sidebar. Connect one app you use at work by signing in. Then add that app's node to a workflow, pick the card you just made, and **send one test message to yourself**. If the message arrives, the card works.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now connect one work app to n8n and make it add a row or send a message.
